data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Back
data.comment: Note on the arrow that goes back to the screen before.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Close
data.comment: Note on the same arrow on the first screen, where there is nothing to go back to.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Undo
data.comment: Note on the undo arrow. {action} is what undoing takes back, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Redo
data.comment: Note on the redo arrow. {action} is what redoing does again, such as "rename".

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Refresh
data.value: Refresh: pick up blocks and buttons changed since this screen opened.
data.comment: Note on the button that reads the blocks again.

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Empty
data.comment: Said under a name being typed, when it is empty and the thing must have a name.

data.name: Sprocket.Rename.Taken
data.comment: Said under a name being typed, when something else already has it.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Broken
data.value: **Something needs mending** Open it to see what.
data.comment: Note on a row's light when it is red.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Ran
data.comment: Note on a row's light while it flashes, just after the thing ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Idle
data.value: **Idle** Lights green when it runs, and red when something in it needs mending.
data.comment: Note on a row's light when it is dark.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.On
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something on. Short: it shares the switch with the next.

data.name: Sprocket.Switch.Off
data.comment: The half of an on/off switch that turns something off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOn
data.comment: Note on an installation's switch while it is off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOff
data.value: Switch this installation off, stopping its sequences
data.comment: Note on an installation's switch while it is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOn
data.value: Switch this logic system on, locking it against changes.
data.comment: Note on a logic system's switch when it is off.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOff
data.value: Switch this logic system off, stopping its sequences and unlocking it for changes.
data.comment: Note on a logic system's switch when it is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOn
data.value: Switch on every installation of this blueprint
data.comment: Note on a blueprint's switch when it is off. Each of them runs where its own switch is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintFirst
data.comment: Note on an installation's switch while its blueprint is switched off, when it cannot be pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOff
data.value: Switch off every installation of this blueprint
data.comment: Note on a blueprint's switch when it is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Title
data.comment: Heading of the first screen. {name} is the grid's name, which is pressed to rename it, so the words either side of it are drawn around it, and the name is always shown exactly as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NameAbout
data.value: This grid's name, as the game shows it everywhere. Renaming it here renames the grid.
data.comment: Note on the grid's name in the heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.New
data.comment: Button, after a plus that means add, that adds a new logic system. A logic system is a set of sequences that work together, such as an airlock's.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NewAbout
data.value: Start a new logic system on this construct.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.OpenAbout
data.value: Open **{name}** to see and change what it does.
data.comment: Note on a logic system's row on the home screen; {name} is the system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.OpenInstanceAbout
data.value: Open **{name}** to choose the blocks it uses.
data.comment: Note on the row of a logic system made from a blueprint, on the home screen; {name} is the system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Load
data.comment: Button that opens the library, which holds the backups and the blueprints. Also the library's heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.PlainHeading
data.comment: Heading over the logic systems of their own on the home screen; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.BlueprintsHeading
data.comment: Heading over the blueprints on the home screen, under the logic systems of their own; shown in capitals.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.LoadAbout
data.value: The **library**: the blueprints on this construct and in storage, and the automation of constructs that are lost.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Empty
data.comment: Said where the list of logic systems would be, when there are none.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprint
data.comment: Button on a logic system's row that makes it a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprintAbout
data.value: Turn this into a **blueprint**, so it can be installed again on other blocks. This one becomes its first installation.
data.comment: Note on the button above.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.EditBlueprint
data.value: Opens the **{name}** blueprint, to change what starts its sequences and what they do. Every installation of it changes with it.
data.comment: Note on the row over the logic systems made from a blueprint. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.LibraryUnbuilt
data.value: Not built yet. Blueprints will be imported and exported here.
data.comment: Said on the blueprint library while it is not built.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnother
data.comment: Adds another installation of a blueprint: its blocks, chosen on the configuration panel. Shown after a plus, as the last line under a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnotherAbout
data.value: Install the **{name}** blueprint on another set of blocks, and choose which blocks it uses.
data.comment: Note on the row above. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Running
data.comment: Said on a logic system's row while any of its sequences runs.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Numbered
data.comment: What a logic system is called when it has no name and its blocks share none. {number} is its number.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Instance
data.comment: What one of the logic systems made from a blueprint is called when it has no name of its own. {name} is the blueprint's, {number} which one it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.System
data.comment: Asked before a logic system is deleted, with its name under it.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Blueprint
data.value: This deletes the {name} blueprint and every installation of it, and cannot be undone. Type {name} to go ahead.
data.comment: Over the box a blueprint's name is typed into to delete it; the button beside the box does nothing until the name is typed. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Instance
data.comment: Asked before one of the logic systems made from a blueprint is deleted, with its name under it. Only that one goes.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.InstanceKept
data.value: The **{name}** blueprint and its other installations are kept. This cannot be undone.
data.comment: Said on the answer that deletes one of the logic systems made from a blueprint. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Keep
data.comment: The answer that deletes nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Confirm
data.comment: The answer that deletes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Delete.Final
data.comment: Said on the answer that deletes.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NameAbout
data.comment: Note on a logic system's name, in the heading of its own screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Blueprint
data.comment: Said after a blueprint's name in the heading of its screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin in the header of a logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteInstallation
data.comment: The bin on an installation's row.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteBlueprint
data.value: Delete this blueprint, and every installation of it
data.comment: Note on the bin in the header of a blueprint's logic system screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EditPanel
data.comment: Button on a blueprint's logic system screen that opens the panel its blocks are chosen on, to set up its slots and description.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EditPanelAbout
data.value: Set up the description and slots everyone filling in this blueprint sees.
data.comment: Note on the button that opens a blueprint's configuration panel.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Using
data.comment: Leads the name of the logic system whose blocks every sentence on the screen names: the system's own, or for a blueprint a list of the blocksets made from it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.UsingAbout
data.value: Pick an installation of this blueprint, to see its blocks in the sentences below.
data.comment: Note on the list of logic systems made from a blueprint, on the blueprint's logic system screen.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Triggers
data.comment: Heading over a logic system's triggers: what starts its sequences.

data.name: Sprocket.System.When
data.comment: Button that adds a trigger started by something happening to a block.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Every
data.comment: Button that adds a trigger started on a timer.

data.name: Sprocket.System.WhenAbout
data.value: Add a trigger that starts on a button or toolbar press, or when a block's value changes.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a trigger started by something happening.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EveryAbout
data.value: Start a sequence repeatedly, on a timed interval.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a trigger started on a timer.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Sequences
data.comment: Heading over a logic system's sequences: the named runs of steps its triggers start.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NewSequence
data.comment: Button, after a plus that means add, that adds a sequence with nothing to start it yet.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NewSequenceAbout
data.value: Add a sequence: steps that run in order. Give it a trigger to start it.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NoSequences
data.comment: Said in place of the list of sequences while a logic system has none.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Copy
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off, with nothing to start it.
data.comment: Note on the copy mark of a sequence that a trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.CopyUnstarted
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off.
data.comment: Note on the copy mark of a sequence nothing starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.OpenSequence
data.value: Open **{name}** to see and change its steps.
data.comment: Note on a sequence's row on the logic system screen; {name} is the sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Live
data.comment: Badge on a trigger while what it watches for is true at this instant, such as a door standing open.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin at the end of a trigger's row.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.BlocksAbout
data.comment: Note on the block a trigger's sentence names.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.WhatAbout
data.value: Choose what happens to the block to start this.
data.comment: Note on what happens to the block, in a trigger's sentence.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.DoesAbout
data.comment: Note on what a trigger's sentence says it does.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.RateAbout
data.comment: Note on how often an Every trigger runs.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.TargetsAbout
data.value: Choose which blocks this trigger acts on.
data.comment: Note on the blocks a trigger's own task acts on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NameAbout
data.comment: Note on a sequence's name, in the heading of its own screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomething
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step acting on blocks. The ellipsis says it asks which before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Wait
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step waiting a length of time. The ellipsis says it asks how long before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomethingAbout
data.value: Add a task: run an action on blocks, or set one of their values.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a task to a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitAbout
data.value: Add a step that waits a while before the next one.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a wait to a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Held
data.comment: Said in place of the buttons that add steps while another player is editing. {holder} is that player's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Delete
data.comment: Note on the bin beside a sequence's switch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteQuestion
data.comment: Asked before a sequence is deleted, with what it does under it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteStep
data.comment: Note on the bin at the end of a step's row.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ActionAbout
data.comment: Note on the action a step's sentence names.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BlocksAbout
data.value: Choose which blocks this step acts on.
data.comment: Note on the blocks a step's sentence names.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ValuesAbout
data.value: Change the value it is given.
data.comment: Note on a value a step's sentence gives.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.LengthAbout
data.comment: Note on a wait's length.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DragStep
data.comment: Note on a step's drag handle.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.PauseStep
data.value: Pause this step. The sequence skips it until it is resumed.
data.comment: Note on the pause mark on a step's row, while the step runs.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.UnpauseStep
data.value: Paused: the sequence skips this step. Press to resume it.
data.comment: Note on the pause mark on a step's row, lit while the step is paused.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBusy
data.comment: Said while a sequence was started and did not run because it was already running. {busy} is how many times.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedOff
data.comment: Said while a sequence was started and did not run because it was switched off. {off} is how many times.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SkippedBoth
data.comment: The two above at once.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitQuestion
data.comment: Title of the question that chooses how long a waiting step waits.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitTypedAbout
data.comment: Note on the box a length of wait is typed into.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitTypeFirst
data.value: Type a whole number of ticks first.
data.comment: Note on the button that takes a typed wait, while nothing is typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Different
data.value: This block holds a program from a different version.
data.comment: Banner on the first screen when the block's program was written by a version that cannot be read.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.DifferentDetail
data.value: This version cannot read it, so this screen starts empty. The block keeps the old program until you change something here. Then it is gone for good.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Broken
data.value: This block holds a program with an error in it.
data.comment: Banner on every screen when the block's program has an error in its text, so none of it was loaded.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.BrokenDetail
data.value: None of it runs, and this screen starts empty. Edit the text to mend it. The block keeps the old program until you change something here. Then it is gone for good.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Mend
data.comment: Button on the banner above that opens the program's text, where the error can be mended.

data.name: Sprocket.Script.Title
data.comment: Heading of the screen that shows the program as text, where it can be edited by hand, and the way in to it.

data.name: Sprocket.Script.Apply
data.comment: Button that reads the text on the screen above and, where it has no error, puts it in place of the program.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Trouble
data.comment: Shown under the banner's detail. {trouble} is what went wrong, in the reader's own words, which are not translated.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Replace
data.comment: Button that replaces the program that could not be read, on the banner and as an answer to the question below.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Question
data.value: Replace the program this block holds? The one that could not be read will be gone.
data.comment: Asked before the first change that replaces a program that could not be read.

data.name: Sprocket.Salvage.Keep
data.comment: Answer to the question above that changes nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Holder
data.comment: Banner when somebody else is editing the same block. {holder} is their name.

data.name: Sprocket.Lease.Detail
data.value: Only one person can edit at a time. Reopen this once they're done to make changes.
data.comment: Shown when the banner above is opened.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Starts
data.comment: Asked on picking a button that another trigger already has. {block} is the button panel, {sequence} the sequence it starts, {blockset} the logic system or blockset it starts it on.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Stops
data.comment: The same, where the other trigger stops its sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Acts
data.comment: The same, where the other trigger acts on its blocks itself rather than starting a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.Elsewhere
data.value: Button {button} of **{block}** already does something else.
data.comment: Asked on picking a button whose slot holds something no trigger here put there: the game's own action, or another block's automation. {button} is the button's number, from 1.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.TakeOver
data.comment: The answer that gives the button to what is being made, taking it from what had it.

data.name: Sprocket.Button.LeaveAlone
data.comment: The answer that leaves the button as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Search
data.comment: Hint in the box that narrows a column of a pick, or its list of kinds, by typing.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Done
data.comment: Button at the right end of the header that finishes the screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.DoneAbout
data.comment: Note on Done on a screen whose changes are kept as they are made.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneFirst
data.value: Choose something in every column first.
data.comment: Note on Done while it cannot be pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneAbout
data.value: Use what is chosen, and go back.
data.comment: Note on Done in a picker, once it can be pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Back
data.comment: Note on the column that turns a pick back to its page before.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Next
data.comment: Note on the column that turns a pick on to its page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ClearTyped
data.comment: Note on the cross that empties a box that narrows a list.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryKind
data.comment: Note on the cross that takes away the kind a list of blocks is narrowed to.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AllShown
data.comment: Line over a list of blocks showing every one. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomeShown
data.comment: Line over a list of blocks narrowed to some of them. {shown} is how many are shown, {count} how many there are.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Anything
data.comment: The entry in the list of kinds that narrows to no kind at all.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KindAbout
data.value: Show only one kind of block.
data.comment: Note on the line that opens the list of kinds of block.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepQuestion
data.comment: Asked on leaving a pick that has changed what it opened on.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KeepThem
data.comment: Answer to the question above that finishes the pick.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DiscardThem
data.comment: Answer to the question above that leaves without finishing.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Blocks
data.comment: Title of the column of blocks in a pick.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksHappen
data.value: Nothing here has anything that can happen to it.
data.comment: Where the column of blocks is empty, picking what starts something.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatToCheck
data.comment: Heading of the column listing what an if can check of the chosen blocks.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingChecked
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can be checked.
data.comment: Said in the column of what to check where the chosen blocks share nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksChecked
data.value: Nothing here has anything that can be checked.
data.comment: Said in the column of blocks where nothing on the construct can be checked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NoBlocksDone
data.value: Nothing here has anything that can be done to it.
data.comment: Where the column of blocks is empty, picking what a step does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatHappens
data.comment: Title of the column of what can happen to the blocks picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatToDo
data.comment: Title of the column of what can be done to the blocks picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingHappens
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can happen to them.
data.comment: Where the column of what happens is empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NothingDone
data.value: Those blocks have nothing in common that can be done to them.
data.comment: Where the column of what to do is empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.WhatItDoes
data.comment: Title of the column choosing what a trigger does.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NonePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where none is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.OnePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where one is picked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SomePicked
data.comment: Under the column of blocks, where several are picked. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AnyOne
data.comment: Choice over the blocks that any one of them is enough.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.AllOfThem
data.comment: Choice over the blocks that all of them are needed together.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Values
data.comment: Heading over a block's values, in the terminal's way of listing what it offers.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ToolbarActions
data.comment: Heading over a block's actions, in the terminal's way of listing what it offers.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Organized
data.comment: Tab showing what a block offers as Sprocket groups and words it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Terminal
data.comment: Tab showing what a block offers as the block itself declares it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Shared
data.value: Showing only what the picked blocks share
data.comment: Note over what several blocks offer.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Pending
data.value: Support for this block is still being worked on, so some of what it offers may be doubled, missing or oddly named.
data.comment: Note over what a block offers, before the block has been checked.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Partial
data.value: Support for this block is only partly done, so some of what it offers may still be doubled, missing or oddly named.
data.comment: Note over what a block offers, where the block has been checked in part.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Waits
data.value: This takes time to finish. The sequence waits until it is done before going on to the next step.
data.comment: Note on the mark beside something done that a step waits for.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Run
data.comment: Choice that a trigger runs the sequence chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Stop
data.comment: Choice that a trigger stops the sequence chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.RunAbout
data.comment: Note on the answer that makes a trigger start a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StopAbout
data.comment: Note on the answer that makes a trigger stop a sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleAction
data.comment: Choice that a trigger does one thing to some blocks, chosen on the page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleActionAbout
data.value: Do a single task on some blocks, without a sequence.
data.comment: Note on the choice of a trigger doing a task of its own.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SingleTask
data.comment: Title of the picker for a trigger's own task.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NewSequence
data.comment: Choice that a trigger runs a sequence made for it.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.NewSequenceAbout
data.value: Make a new sequence for this trigger to start.
data.comment: Note on the choice of a new sequence for a trigger.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Sequences
data.comment: Heading over the sequences a trigger may run or stop.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOftenQuestion
data.comment: Title of the page choosing how often a timer fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HowOften
data.comment: Title of the column of rates a timer fires at.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryTick
data.comment: The fastest rate a timer fires at.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Rate
data.comment: A rate a timer fires at. {name} is its word, such as steady; {ticks} how many ticks apart.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameAbout
data.comment: Note on a blueprint's name at the head of its screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Parts
data.comment: Heading over a blueprint's slots, where each is filled with blocks.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Panel
data.comment: Heading of a blueprint's configuration panel while it is being set up: the slots and words everyone filling a blockset made from the blueprint sees.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.PanelFor
data.comment: After "Configuration panel" in its heading. {name} is the blueprint's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.PanelAbout
data.value: Shown to anyone setting up, or changing, something made from this blueprint.
data.comment: Under the heading of a configuration panel being set up.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillOne
data.comment: Beside the heading over a blockset's slots, where one slot that needs a block has none.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.StillMany
data.comment: Beside the heading over a blockset's slots. {count} is how many slots that need a block have none, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.FromLead
data.comment: Before the blueprint's name in the heading of a logic system made from it; the name opens the blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.FromAfter
data.comment: After the blueprint's name in that heading, or empty for nothing.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Gone
data.comment: Beside a slot whose block is no longer on the construct. {name} is what the block was called.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.Description
data.comment: Heading over the box a blueprint's description is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.DescriptionHint
data.value: What this blueprint does, and what whoever fills it in needs to know.
data.comment: In the empty box a blueprint's description is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.AboutHint
data.comment: In the empty box what a slot is for is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameBoxAbout
data.value: The slot's name, as everyone filling in this blueprint sees it.
data.comment: Note on the box a slot's name is typed into.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.RequiredAbout
data.value: Whether an installation of this blueprint may leave this slot empty.
data.comment: Note on the switch between required and optional.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Preview
data.comment: Button that shows rich text as it will read, in place of the box it is written in.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.Edit

data.comment: Label on the programmable block that keeps the automation, shown only in developer mode.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Action
data.comment: The block's toolbar action, as the game lists it.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Refused
data.value: This block's automation cannot be edited.
data.comment: The game's message when the editor cannot open.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Saved
data.comment: Under a backup in the library. {time} is the date and time it was taken.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.NoneSaved
data.value: None yet. A blueprint saved here goes wherever you go.
data.comment: Said where no blueprint is saved.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.OnConstructs
data.comment: Heading in the library over the blueprints on the player's constructs, and the constructs that are lost.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ThisConstruct
data.comment: Line in the library over the blueprints on the construct it was opened on. {name} is the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.NoneHere
data.comment: Said in the library where the construct has no blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.NoInstallations
data.comment: Under a blueprint in the library that is on the construct with no installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.OneInstallation
data.comment: Under a blueprint in the library that is on the construct with one installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Installations
data.comment: Under a blueprint in the library that is on the construct. {count} is how many installations, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Lost
data.value: Lost {time}. Its automation is kept here.
data.comment: Under a construct in the library that is gone from the world. {time} is when its automation was last saved.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ForgetLost
data.comment: Note on the bin of a lost construct in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ForgetLostQuestion
data.value: Forget the automation of this lost construct?
data.comment: Asked before forgetting a lost construct's automation; the construct's name follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.InStorage
data.comment: Heading in the library over the blueprints the player keeps, which go wherever they go.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.SavedBy
data.comment: Under a blueprint in the library that somebody else made. {name} is who, {time} when it was put in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Forget
data.comment: Note on the bin of a blueprint in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ForgetQuestion
data.comment: Asked before deleting a blueprint from storage; its name follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Here
data.comment: Beside the switch in the library that puts the chosen blueprint on the construct, or takes it off.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.PutOn
data.value: Put this blueprint on this construct, ready for its first installation.
data.comment: Note on the switch in the library, where the blueprint is not on the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOff
data.value: Take this blueprint off this construct. Its copy in storage is kept, brought up to date.
data.comment: Note on the switch in the library, and on the minus of a blueprint on the home screen, where the blueprint has no installation and is in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.HeldOne
data.value: 1 installation on this construct. Remove it from the home screen first.
data.comment: Note on the switch in the library, which cannot be pressed while the blueprint has an installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Held
data.value: {count} installations on this construct. Remove them from the home screen first.
data.comment: Note on the switch in the library, which cannot be pressed while the blueprint has installations. {count} is how many, always more than one.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Save
data.comment: Button in the library that keeps a copy of the chosen blueprint for every world.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.SaveAbout
data.value: Keep a copy in storage. It goes wherever you go.
data.comment: Note on the button that saves a blueprint to the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Update
data.comment: Button in the library that puts the blueprint on the construct in place of the copy in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.UpdateAbout
data.value: Put this blueprint in place of the stored copy.
data.comment: Note on the button that updates the library's copy of a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Same
data.value: The stored copy is the same as this one.
data.comment: Note on the update button, which cannot be pressed while the copies are the same.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.By
data.comment: Line under the chosen blueprint's name in the library. {name} is who made it.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ByChanged
data.comment: Line under the chosen blueprint's name in the library. {name} is who made it, {time} when it was last changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Changed
data.comment: Line under the chosen blueprint's name in the library, where nobody is named. {time} is when it was last changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.InstallationsHeading
data.comment: Heading in the library over the chosen blueprint's installations on the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Systems
data.comment: Heading in the library over the logic systems a lost construct had.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.RemoveFirst
data.value: Remove its installations first, then take it off the construct.
data.comment: Note on the quiet minus of a blueprint on the home screen, while it has installations.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Unreadable
data.comment: In place of the status of a blueprint in the library whose text will not read; what is wrong is shown beside the list.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Copy
data.comment: Button in the library that puts a copy of the chosen blueprint on the construct, as a blueprint of its own.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.CopyAbout
data.value: Put a copy on this construct, as a blueprint of its own: changing the copy leaves this one as it is.
data.comment: Note on the button that makes a copy of a blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.CopyName
data.comment: What a copy of a blueprint is called. {name} is the blueprint copied, {number} the first number from 2 nothing is called yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Deletes
data.value: Delete this blueprint. It is not in storage, so this is its only copy.
data.comment: Note on the bin of a blueprint on the home screen, and on the switch in the library, where the blueprint has no installation and is not in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOffQuestion
data.value: Take this blueprint off this construct?
data.comment: Asked before taking a blueprint in storage off the construct; its name follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOffKept
data.value: Its copy in storage is kept, brought up to date.
data.comment: Under the question about taking a blueprint off the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOffKeep
data.comment: Answer to the question about taking a blueprint off the construct that leaves it on.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOffConfirm
data.comment: Answer to the question about taking a blueprint off the construct that takes it off.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameTaken
data.comment: Under a slot's name box while what is typed is another slot's name. {name} is the name typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameEmpty
data.comment: Under a slot's name box while it is empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameKeptTaken
data.value: Not renamed: another slot is already called {name}.
data.comment: Under a slot's name box after a name another slot has was typed and the box left; the slot keeps its name. {name} is the name typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameKeptEmpty
data.value: Not renamed: a slot needs a name.
data.comment: Under a slot's name box after it was left empty; the slot keeps its name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Run
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step running another sequence. The ellipsis says it asks which before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunAbout
data.value: Add a step that runs another sequence of this system.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a step running another sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunQuestion
data.comment: Title of the list of the system's other sequences, one of which a new step runs.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunNone
data.value: This system has no other sequence to run.
data.comment: Said in place of the list of sequences to run where the system has no other sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Stop
data.comment: Button under a sequence's steps, after a plus that means add, that adds a step stopping another sequence. The ellipsis says it asks which before it adds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StopAbout
data.value: Add a step that stops another sequence of this system.
data.comment: Note on the button that adds a step stopping another sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.If
data.comment: The button that adds an if to the end of a sequence: the steps dragged into it run only where what it checks holds.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.IfAbout
data.value: Add an if: steps dragged into it run only where what it checks holds.
data.comment: Tooltip for the button that adds an if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseIf
data.comment: The button under an if that adds a branch checking something else, tried where nothing before it held.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseIfAbout
data.value: Add a branch that checks something else, where nothing above it held.
data.comment: Tooltip for the button that adds an otherwise if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Otherwise
data.comment: The button under an if that adds its last branch, run where nothing above it held.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseAbout
data.value: Add a last branch, which runs where nothing above it held.
data.comment: Tooltip for the button that adds an otherwise.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseTestAbout
data.value: Make this an otherwise if, which checks something first.
data.comment: Tooltip for the button on an otherwise that gives it something to check, which makes it an otherwise if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StateAbout
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of an if that says what it checks of its blocks, such as is closed.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RemoveIf
data.comment: Asked when the bin on an if is pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RemoveBranch
data.comment: Asked when the bin on an otherwise or otherwise if is pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.KeepSteps
data.comment: The answer that removes only the if or branch line, leaving its steps where they are.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteSteps
data.value: Delete the steps in it too
data.comment: The answer that removes the if or branch with every step in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StopQuestion
data.comment: Title of the list of the system's other sequences, one of which a new step stops.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StopNone
data.value: This system has no other sequence to stop.
data.comment: Said in place of the list of sequences to stop where the system has no other sequence.
